model.rationale: The D+21 district, Khanna's enormous financial edge over a challenger with under $1,000 on hand, and markets pricing him near 97% all point to a lopsided incumbent win, and nothing in the evidence contradicts that picture.
model.watch: Any sign of a well-funded challenger effort or outside spending on Tandon's behalf would warrant revisiting, though nothing currently suggests one will materialize.

overview:
California's 17th District sits deep in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the party, and Ro Khanna has held the seat since 2017. He enters the general election with an overwhelming resource advantage: more than $16.9 million on hand after raising $13.7 million, against about $37,000 raised and under $1,000 in cash for Republican Ritesh Tandon. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, and no expert raters have ranked it, which is itself telling about how competitive it is seen to be. Prediction markets price Khanna's chances at about 97 percent. The expected margin is roughly 26 points, with uncertainty near eight points given the absence of polling. Barring an unforeseen development, the district appears set to return its incumbent by a wide margin.
